tasks.title: Scaffold runner and mocker projects
tasks.description: Create two .NET 10 console projects. Runner/Runner.csproj references QaaS.Runner and QaaS.Common.Assertions (the runner uses the built-in HttpStatus + HermeticByExpectedOutputCount assertions; the data generator is CUSTOM so no QaaS.Common.Generators is required). Mocker/Mocker.csproj references QaaS.Mocker and QaaS.Common.Processors. Each Program.cs is the exact one-liner QaaS.Runner.Bootstrap.New(args).Run(); and QaaS.Mocker.Bootstrap.New(args).Run(); respectively. OutputType=Exe; copy *.qaas.yaml (runner) and *.mocker.yaml (mocker) to output.
acceptanceCriteria: dotnet build exits 0 for both projects

tasks.title: Author the custom IGenerator hook
tasks.description: Write Runner/SequentialIdGenerator.cs in the Runner namespace: a custom generator 'SequentialIdGenerator' deriving from BaseGenerator<SequentialIdConfig>. SequentialIdConfig is a record with a nullable [Required] uint? Count. Override Generate(IImmutableList<SessionData> sessionDataList, IImmutableList<DataSource> dataSourceList) to yield return Count items, each a Data<object> whose Body is the UTF-8 bytes of a deterministic JSON object like {"id":N} for N = 1..Count. Use the copy-verbatim runner-hook using header (Data<T> and SessionData are in two separate namespaces). Must compile.
rubric: Proper BaseGenerator<T> inheritance and exact Generate signature
Config is a record with nullable + [Required] Count
acceptanceCriteria: dotnet build succeeds with the new generator

tasks.title: Author runner + mocker YAML and verify end-to-end
tasks.description: Author Runner/orders.qaas.yaml: a DataSource whose Generator is the custom SequentialIdGenerator (GeneratorConfiguration: { Count: 3 }); a Session with a Transaction that does an Http POST to the mocker (BaseAddress http://127.0.0.1, Port = the port contract (8112), Route orders with NO leading slash, Method Post, DataSourceNames referencing the generator data source, TimeoutMs 5000); and Assertions: HttpStatus 200 (OutputNames = the transaction name) PLUS HermeticByExpectedOutputCount (ExpectedCount: 3, OutputNames = the transaction name) so the assertion is not vacuous. Author Mocker/orders.mocker.yaml: an Http server on the contract port with an Endpoint Path /orders whose POST action returns HTTP 200 (a StaticResponseProcessor stub is fine). A Transaction MUST carry a protocol block (Http) - a Transaction with DataSourceNames but no Http/protocol block fails with 'Missing supported type in transaction'.
rubric: Custom generator wired by simple class name
Transaction has an Http protocol block (not generator-only)
Hermetic count guard present alongside HttpStatus

verify.cmd: $m = Start-Process dotnet -ArgumentList 'run','-c','Release','--','run','orders.mocker.yaml' -WorkingDirectory '..\\Mocker' -PassThru; $ok=$false; foreach($i in 1..40){ try{(New-Object Net.Sockets.TcpClient('127.0.0.1',8112)).Close();$ok=$true;break}catch{Start-Sleep 2}}; if(-not $ok){Stop-Process -Id $m.Id -Force; exit 9}; dotnet run -c Release -- run orders.qaas.yaml; $code=$LASTEXITCODE; Stop-Process -Id $m.Id -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; exit $code

acceptanceCriteria: Template verification passes for both YAMLs
End-to-end run exits 0 (custom generator feeds 3 POSTs, all 200, hermetic count satisfied)
failureModes: Transaction with DataSourceNames but no Http block (Missing supported type)
Vacuous HttpStatus with no count guard

goalOneSentence: Implement a custom QaaS IGenerator (deterministic sequential ids) and prove it end-to-end by POSTing the generated data to a live mocker and asserting HttpStatus 200 + a hermetic output count.
portContract: This sprint's mocker MUST listen on HTTP port 8112 and the runner Transaction MUST target http://127.0.0.1:8112 (set the mocker server Port: 8112 and the runner BaseAddress/Port to 8112). Do NOT use the 8080 default from Fact Base examples - use 8112 exactly, or the live end-to-end run cannot connect.
